Argentina’s Shelled Peanuts Displace China in
Key European Markets.
Shelled Peanuts Exports to Europe, Ukraine, and Russia

Argentina’s share of shelled peanut exports to key European markets
doubled between 2004 and 2007 in response to growing production,
improved quality, and attractive pricing. Much of gains in these markets
have come at the expense of China whose market share has dropped from
40 percent to 20 percent. Difficulty in meeting the EU’s strict aflatoxin
limits along with elimination of the rebate of the EU’s 5 percent VAT have
contributed to the decline. Reduced peanut production and increased
demand in China have also played a role in reducing exports to the region.
US sales to Europe have been relatively unaffected by the gains made by
Argentina with market share holding steady near 10 percent.
Approved by the World Agricultural Outlook Board/USDA

TRADE CHANGES IN 2009/10
• U.S. soybean exports are boosted 0.7 million tons to a record 39.3 million supported
by unusually large shipments in March despite strong competition from South
America.
• Brazil’s soybean exports are up 0.7 million tons to 26.3 million supported by seasonal
competitiveness in key markets, particularly in China.
• China’s soybean imports are up 1.0 million tons to a record 43.5 million due to larger
crush demand.
• China’s rapeseed imports are up 0.3 million tons to 1.8 million in response to
continued large volume coming from Canada.
• Japan’s soybean imports are cut 0.3 million tons to 3.6 million due to slow crush
demand and are partially offset by larger soy meal imports.
• India’s soybean meal exports are down 0.3 million tons to 2.2 million due to reduced
crush demand.
